transcript: Hi, this is State Representative Jim Walsh. Transparency and trust are essential to good government, good law, and good public policy. That's why the four initiatives on your general election ballot this November are so important. Beyond the specific problem that each initiative fixes, three are tax reforms. Our state constitution says it right at the start. All political power is inherent in the people. That's why it's so troubling that a gang of partisan special interest groups recently attacked the four initiatives in court. Their lawsuits tried to remove the initiatives from the November ballot. Thankfully, the state supreme court rejected the attack. But there's more to the story. The state attorney general's office failed to notify the initiative's sponsors, supporters, and the people of Washington about the partisan attacks. The AG kept the whole thing very quiet, which is unusual. Why? Maybe because the partisan special interest groups launching the attacks are also political allies of the AG. Whatever the reason, this secretiveness about an attempt to remove the people's voice from the upcoming election is not transparent and does not inspire trust. Law shouldn't be made in the dark, hidden furtively from the people's view. There's been too much of that in recent years. bills passed in the middle of the night, bureaucratic rules made without public input, court decisions made without the people most effective being told. To fix what's broken in Washington, we need to restore transparency. We need to restore the people's trust. That's what our Constitution says, and it's what the initiatives do.
